Double Peaking Phenomena in Pharmacokinetic Disposition Revisited. Multiple peaking in pharmacokinetics refers to the occurrence of two or more peaks of drug plasma concentrations following a single dose administration. It complicates interpretation of pharmacokinetics parameters and influences clinical decision-making regarding drug efficacy and bioequivalence. Exploring the multiple effects of nifedipine and captopril administration in spontaneously hypertensive rats through pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic analyses. This study assessed the pharmacokinetics (PKs) and pharmacodynamics (PDs) of two antihypertensive drugs, nifedipine and captopril, by exploring their main (blood pressure [BP]) and secondary effects (heart rate [HR] and QT interval [QT]) in spontaneously hypertensive rats.
